articles.title: 'Dealing with you was horrendous': Former NSW coach Anthony Stuart hits back at Usman Khawaja amid Sandpapergate controversy
articles.summary: Former New South Wales coach Anthony Stuart has responded strongly to criticism from retired Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his autobiography.
articles.body: Former New South Wales coach Anthony Stuart has responded strongly to criticism from retired Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his autobiography. Stuart took to social media to share his side of the story and recalled several incidents from Khawaja's time with the NSW team.Khawaja had written about his experience under Stuart before moving to Queensland to play Sheffield Shield cricket in 2012. He questioned the support he received from his former coach and said he could not build a good relationship with him.“Anthony Stuart was a good enough guy but as a coach he didn’t do anything for me,” Khawaja wrote.“I tried so hard to build a rapport, talk to him about himself or his family and I just got nothing," he wrote.Stuart, who played three one-day internationals for Australia, said he had already shared his views about Khawaja privately with friends. He also responded to the batter's comments about their relationship.Stuart said he did not remember Khawaja asking him about his family or personal life. He also apologised if his response had not been what the batter expected.“My memory is pretty good, but apparently I didn’t disclose that, or anything else about my private life, to you. I certainly don’t remember you ever asking about my family, but if we did, I apologise for not engaging to your liking," Stuart wrote.Stuart recalls issues during trainingThe former NSW coach also spoke about what he described as Khawaja's “regular complaining” during his playing days. He pointed to an incident during training when the batter continued to wear his pads after finishing his batting session.“Constantly walking around training with your pads on after batting,” he wrote.“Pretty hard to then bowl to the teammates that had just spent time bowling to you. “Or was it just a coincidence?"Dispute over batting positionStuart also recalled a disagreement over Khawaja's batting position in a Sheffield Shield match in Tasmania. He claimed Khawaja and his manager had strongly objected to him opening the batting for NSW.The team at the time included established batters such as Steve Smith, Simon Katich and Phil Hughes. Stuart said Smith was the team's best batter and should bat at No. 3. Smith went on to score 98 in that match.“You, and then your manager at the time, having a massive tantrum about you having to open the batting for NSW in a shield game in Tasmania, when the best player ‘should bat three’," he said.“Hate to break it to you, but they were all better players than you. Your manager was right, our best player should bat three. He (Smith) did. He got 98. Dealing with you, and your manager back then, and again I paraphrase you, was just horrendous,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'He's breaking the door down': Former cricketer's big praise for Priyansh Arya after record-breaking 181 in SMAT
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India domestic cricket stalwart Priyank Panchal has thrown his weight behind Priyansh Arya's potential India call-up after the young
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India domestic cricket stalwart Priyank Panchal has thrown his weight behind Priyansh Arya's potential India call-up after the young Delhi and Punjab Kings batter produced a record-breaking knock in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT), saying he is "breaking the door down" with his performances.Arya smashed a sensational 181 off just 68 balls against Tamil Nadu on Tuesday, becoming the highest-scoring Indian batter in T20 cricket history. His innings, featuring seven fours and 19 sixes at a strike rate of 266, helped Delhi post a massive 275/5 in 20 overs.The 25-year-old surpassed KL Rahul's previous Indian record of 152 not out off 67 balls, scored for Delhi Capitals against Punjab Kings at the Arun Jaitley Stadium earlier this year. Rahul's knock was also the first 150-plus individual score by an Indian in IPL history.Taking to X, Panchal praised Arya's progress across formats and pointed to his performances in the IPL, domestic cricket and India A assignments as evidence of his growing credentials."Priyansh Arya has been in sensational form in the IPL. And he has been rewarded for that with India A appearances too. Now, with such SMAT performances, where he’s scoring 180+ runs, he’s breaking the door down. Don’t forget he got a fine century in Ranji Trophy too this season!" Panchal wrote.IPL impact, Ranji Trophy returns strengthen Arya's caseArya has been among the most exciting young batters in Indian cricket. In the 2026 IPL season, he scored 364 runs in 13 innings for PBKS at an average of 28 and a strike rate of 211.62, including three half-centuries.He had announced himself during PBKS' 2025 runners-up campaign, finishing with 475 runs in 17 innings at a strike rate of nearly 180, including a century and two fifties.His red-ball numbers have also been impressive. In three Ranji Trophy appearances for Delhi this season, Arya has scored 311 runs across four innings at an average of 77.75, including a century and a half-century. His highest score was 199 against Gujarat.Arya has also featured regularly for India A. He scored 101 off 84 balls against Australia A on his debut in October 2025 and made 137 runs in four innings during the 50-over tri-series in June. More recently, he scored 49 off 45 balls against Australia A in October.Arya enters record books with stunning SMAT assaultThe latest innings has placed Arya among the biggest individual performers in T20 history. His 181 is the second-highest individual score in the format, behind South Africa's Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who made 188 off 79 balls for Titans against Knights in the CSA Pro20 Cup in October.Arya also equalled Finn Allen's world record of 19 sixes in a single T20 innings. His score is the highest in SMAT history, surpassing Tilak Varma's 151 for Hyderabad against Meghalaya in November 2024.Delhi's 275/5 was the third-highest total in the tournament's history. Tamil Nadu, in reply, were bowled out for 159 in 18.3 overs, with Digvesh Rathi taking four wickets, Suyash Sharma claiming three and Mayank Yadav picking up two.Arya is also leading the run charts this SMAT season, with 362 runs in six innings at an average of 60.33 and a strike rate of 204.51, including a century and three half-centuries.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Had a feeling I would score a hundred':  India-born Harpreet Bhatia's emotional ton on Guru Nanak Jayanti against India A
articles.summary: An India-born cricketer who once represented the country at the U-19 level and featured in the IPL turned the spotlight on himself with a memorable
articles.body: An India-born cricketer who once represented the country at the U-19 level and featured in the IPL turned the spotlight on himself with a memorable century against India A in the Rising Stars Asia Cup on Tuesday.Harpreet Singh Bhatia, who represented Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh in Indian domestic cricket before becoming a UAE citizen earlier this year, produced a remarkable 130 off 144 deliveries to guide the UAE to 249/8 in their Group B encounter.The 35-year-old, who has also featured in nine IPL matches for franchises including Punjab Kings, Kolkata Knight Riders and Rising Pune Supergiants, held the UAE innings together after the team lost its opening wickets cheaply. His knock featured 12 boundaries and four sixes, as he registered his seventh List A century and surpassed his previous best score of 121.Harpreet Singh Recalls Emotional Century Against IndiaHaving spent a significant part of his cricketing career in India, Harpreet's century against India A carried special significance. The left-hander admitted that scoring runs against a quality opposition like India was a major motivation."There was always motivation to score against a big team. And India is a very good side, and I'm glad that I made it," Harpreet said.He also revealed that he had a special feeling about scoring a century on the occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti."And I had a thought this morning that today is Guru Nanak Jayanti. I got a feeling that I'm going to score a hundred today. So it has come after a very long time on Guru Nanak Jayanti. I want to wish everyone a happy Gurpurab," he added.The former India U-19 player looked comfortable against the India A bowling attack and particularly enjoyed taking on pacer Harshit Rana, whom he struck for a couple of sixes down the ground. One of those maximums came off a slower delivery and also brought up his seventh List A hundred.Arshad Khan Ends Harpreet's Resistance, India A Restrict UAE To 249Harpreet continued to anchor the UAE innings as wickets kept falling at the other end. However, his impressive knock eventually came to an end in the 47th over when left-arm pacer Arshad Khan bowled him for 130 off 144 deliveries.Arshad was the standout performer for India A, finishing with figures of 4/43 in his 10 overs. Harshit Rana, meanwhile, endured an expensive outing, conceding 63 runs in his 10 overs while picking up one wicket. The pacer is also looking to prove his match fitness after returning from injury.Despite Harpreet's century, the other UAE batters struggled to maintain momentum and failed to convert their starts into substantial contributions, allowing India A to restrict them to 249/8 in 50 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ends 12-year wait, smashes 100 off 28 balls to surpass Suresh Raina's famous 87 off 25
articles.summary: Suresh Raina's breathtaking 87 off 25 balls for Chennai Super Kings against Kings XI Punjab in IPL 2014 had remained one of the most iconic power-hitting
articles.body: Suresh Raina's breathtaking 87 off 25 balls for Chennai Super Kings against Kings XI Punjab in IPL 2014 had remained one of the most iconic power-hitting displays in Indian cricket. More than a decade later, teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has produced an innings that has taken the comparison to another level, smashing a sensational 100 off just 28 deliveries for India A against the UAE in the Rising Stars Asia Cup on Tuesday.Raina's extraordinary knock came during the IPL 2014 Qualifier 2 at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on May 30. Chasing a daunting 227-run target, the left-hander went berserk, smashing 12 fours and six sixes at a staggering strike rate of 348. He scored 87 runs in just 25 balls before being run out on the first delivery of the seventh over.His 87-run effort remains the highest individual score inside the six-over powerplay in IPL history. However, Sooryavanshi has now surpassed that tally in a remarkable display of power-hitting, reaching his century in just 28 balls against UAE.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 28-ball carnage against UAEOpening the innings for India A in a 250-run chase, Sooryavanshi launched an astonishing assault on the UAE bowling attack from the very first over.The 15-year-old brought up his half-century in just 16 deliveries, smashing eight sixes in the process. He showed no signs of slowing down and continued to clear the boundary with remarkable ease.Sooryavanshi eventually reached the three-figure mark in just 28 balls, becoming the fastest centurion in List A cricket history. His innings featured 13 sixes and four boundaries, as he dismantled the UAE bowling attack inside the first seven overs. The youngster completed his century by smashing Ibrar Ahmad for a boundary in the seventh over, sparking celebrations in the India A dressing room.Raina's 87 off 25 remains one of the most memorable knocks in IPL history, particularly because of the circumstances in which it came. Chennai Super Kings were chasing 227 against Kings XI Punjab in the second qualifier of IPL 2014. After losing Faf du Plessis early, Raina walked in and immediately took the attack to the opposition.He smashed 12 fours and six sixes, scoring at a strike rate of 348. His extraordinary assault included a 33-run over against Parvinder Awana, which briefly brought CSK back into contention.However, Raina was run out for 87 on the first ball of the seventh over, ending a remarkable innings. CSK eventually finished at 202/7, losing the contest by 24 runs. More than 12 years later, Sooryavanshi has delivered another extraordinary batting spectacle, surpassing Raina's famous 87-run tally in a completely different format and setting.India A's must-win clash Against UAEIndia A entered the contest under pressure after losing their previous Group B encounter against Pakistan Shaheens. The side needed a strong response to keep its qualification hopes alive. Earlier, Harpreet Singh Bhatia had anchored the UAE innings with an impressive 130 off 144 balls, helping his side post 249/8 in 50 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India A complete record-breaking chase, hammer UAE by seven wickets in just 14.2 overs after Sooryavanshi's 204
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages, smashing a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls as India A chased down 250 against the United Arab
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages, smashing a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls as India A chased down 250 against the United Arab Emirates in just 14.2 overs to register a seven-wicket victory in the Rising Stars Asia Cup on Tuesday.Harpreet Singh Bhatia's Century Rescues UAE After Early CollapseUAE skipper Basil Hameed won the toss and opted to bat first, but the decision did not immediately pay dividends as India A struck early with the ball. Harshit Rana removed opener Aryansh Sharma for two, while Arshad Khan dismissed Ansh Tandon for eight to leave UAE struggling at 20/2 inside the first six overs.With the innings in danger of falling apart, Harpreet Singh Bhatia took responsibility and anchored the recovery. The former India U-19 cricketer, who has also featured in the IPL, showed tremendous composure against the India A bowling attack. Harpreet stitched together a crucial 71-run partnership with Muhammad Shahdad, who contributed 28 off 46 deliveries. The left-hander then continued to hold one end together as Ethan D'Souza added 25 off 37 balls.Harpreet eventually brought up a memorable century and continued batting deep into the innings. His 130 off 144 deliveries featured 12 fours and four sixes, making it a career-best List A score. However, Arshad Khan ended his resistance in the 47th over, bowling him for 130. Arshad continued his impressive spell by dismissing Ibrar Ahmad for a duck in the following over.Captain Basil Hameed provided some late resistance with an unbeaten 36 off 36 balls, helping UAE finish at 249/8 in 50 overs.Arshad was the standout bowler for India A, finishing with figures of 4/43 in 10 overs. Harshit Rana conceded 63 runs but picked up one wicket, while Harsh Dubey, Shahbaz Ahmed and Suryansh Shedge also claimed a wicket each.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi goes berserkChasing 250, India A could not have asked for a more explosive start from their opening pair of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma. Sooryavanshi attacked from the very first over, taking on UAE pacer Zahid Ali with three consecutive sixes in the opening over. He continued his assault against Ibrar Ahmad and Basil Hameed, reaching his half-century in just 16 deliveries.Abhishek Sharma joined the six-hitting spree, but his stay was brief as he was dismissed by Ibrar Ahmad for 12 off five balls. Sooryavanshi, however, continued to dominate the UAE attack and brought up his century in just 28 deliveries. The teenager broke Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk's previous record of a 29-ball List A century, creating history with his extraordinary knock.Prabhsimran Singh also failed to make a significant contribution, departing for three off four balls, but the wickets did little to slow Sooryavanshi down. The left-hander continued his assault and reached 150 in just 40 balls, making it one of the most extraordinary power-hitting displays in the history of List A cricket.Sooryavanshi's assault reached another level as he continued to clear the boundary with remarkable ease. He brought up his double century in just 53 deliveries, becoming the fastest batter to score 200 in List A cricket. His final tally of 28 sixes broke the previous record of 26 maximums in a professional cricket innings, held by Hyderabad's Tanmay Agarwal.Sooryavanshi eventually departed for 204 off 53 balls after attempting to clear long-off against Basil Hameed in the 13th over. Aryansh Sharma completed the catch as the UAE captain finally ended the teenage sensation's monumental innings.Rinku Singh finishes the chase as India A seal dominant victoryWith the target almost within reach, Rinku Singh ensured there were no further twists in the contest. He remained unbeaten on 21 off 17 deliveries, while Kumar Kushagra was unbeaten on one. Rinku brought the chase to a close in the 15th over, smashing Basil Hameed for a six over deep mid-wicket as India A reached 254/3 in just 14.2 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I do feel pressure': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opens up after record-breaking double century
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have rewritten the List A record books with a breathtaking 53-ball double century, but the teenager revealed that there was no
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have rewritten the List A record books with a breathtaking 53-ball double century, but the teenager revealed that there was no change in his mindset going into the record-breaking innings against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday.The 15-year-old smashed an astonishing 204 off just 53 deliveries, including 28 sixes, the most ever by a batter in List A cricket, as India A chased down UAE's 250-run target in just 14.2 overs, winning by seven wickets in their Group B encounter in Doha.Sooryavanshi registered the fastest century and double century in List A cricket, reaching the 100-run milestone in just 28 balls before completing his double hundred off 52 deliveries. He also became the first batter to score two List A half-centuries in 16 balls or fewer.Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Sooryavanshi explained that his approach was initially to spend time at the crease after failing to convert his starts in the previous two matches. However, he quickly realised that the surface offered little assistance to the bowlers and decided to back his natural attacking game."In the last two matches, I got set but couldn't convert those starts. So the plan was to go out there and take my time initially. But after facing a ball or two, I felt the bowlers weren't getting much help from the surface, so I backed my strengths," Sooryavanshi said.The left-hander revealed that his focus was simply on assessing the conditions and adjusting his approach accordingly, rather than thinking about records or milestones."There wasn't anything specific on my mind. The only thought was that if the wicket was helping the bowlers, I would take my time and play a longer innings. But thankfully, that wasn't the case. The wicket was good, the ball was coming nicely onto the bat, so I tried to back my game," he added.'Same mindset of trying to bat deep'Despite producing one of the most extraordinary innings in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi insisted that his mindset remained unchanged. He said his priority was always to bat deep and take control of the game once he settled in."Nothing different, sir. It was the same mindset of trying to bat deep. If the game wasn't in my control initially, I would look to take my time. But thankfully, I was able to take control early on, and then I played the game on my terms," he said.Sooryavanshi also spoke about his experience of captaining Bihar, describing it as an enjoyable responsibility. He credited the senior players around him for making the environment comfortable and encouraging open discussions within the team."It was a lot of fun captaining Bihar, and the team is doing quite well too. Hopefully, Bihar continue performing the same way. As far as this team is concerned, I've been around all the senior players for a long time, so I'm very comfortable with them. They make me feel at ease, everyone speaks openly, and whenever they have a suggestion, they share it with me. I listen to everyone," he said.'If I just watch the ball properly, the game will be easy'The teenage batter also revealed the consistent advice he receives from his coaches, particularly Hrishi sir, who has been guiding him since his Under-19 days."Hrishi sir, for example, keeps telling me the same thing before every match. He has been saying this since Under-19. He tells me that if I just watch the ball properly, the game will be easy for me," Sooryavanshi said.Having rediscovered his rhythm against UAE, the youngster is now hoping to carry the momentum into the remaining matches of the tournament."It feels good. I've got my flow back in the game, so I'll try to carry this forward into the remaining matches of the tournament. Hopefully, we win the semi final and reach the final, and I can continue playing with the same flow and in my own way," he added.Interestingly, despite his fearless approach and record-breaking hitting, Sooryavanshi admitted that he does feel pressure while batting. However, he said the nerves usually settle after facing a few deliveries."Absolutely, You do feel a little pressure. It's normal, it's human nature to feel a bit nervous. But after two or four balls, I settle down and get back to normal," he said.India A entered the UAE contest under pressure after losing to Pakistan Shaheens in their previous match and needing a win to strengthen their semi-final qualification hopes. Sooryavanshi's extraordinary innings ensured a dominant response, with the youngster producing a performance that will be remembered for its remarkable collection of records.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chhattisgarh-born, MP-groomed batter Harpreet hits century for UAE
articles.summary: Chhattisgarh-born Harpreet Singh Bhatia scored a century for UAE after rising through MP cricket, later captaining Chhattisgarh and moving to UAE in 2026.
articles.body: Raipur: Chhattisgarh-born batter Harpreet Singh Bhatia scored a century for the UAE on Tuesday, completing a remarkable journey that began in Madhya Pradesh because his home state had no place in Indian cricket’s national structure at the time.Chhattisgarh was a newly formed state in 2000 and had no permanent BCCI membership then. Bhatia, born in Chhattisgarh’s Dallirajhara, moved up through MP’s Under-14, Under-17, Under-19 and Under-23 squads before making his Ranji Trophy debut for them.When Chhattisgarh finally received full BCCI membership in 2016, he went home. He played Ranji Trophy cricket for Chhattisgarh from 2018 to 2024 and captained the side for three consecutive years before the Covid-19 pandemic. He then returned to Madhya Pradesh, where he played until 2026. In the IPL, he played for Kolkata Knight Riders, Pune Warriors India and Punjab Kings.Despite consistent, standout performances in domestic cricket, the 35-year-old saw limited prospects of breaking into the Indian national team. Seeking new opportunities, he moved to the UAE in January 2026, while his wife remained in Dallirajhara, according to his father, garment trader Jashpal Singh Bhatia (65).Bhatia settled in quickly. He began playing in the UAE in February 2026, securing a spot in the national ODI team. articles.title: India A create history with fastest 200-plus chase, quickest team hundred in record-breaking rout of UAE
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's sensational 204 off just 53 balls powered India A to a historic seven-wicket victory over the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's sensational 204 off just 53 balls powered India A to a historic seven-wicket victory over the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Doha on Tuesday. The teenager's extraordinary batting display helped India A chase down a target of 250 in just 14.2 overs, setting multiple team records in the process.Quickest chase of 200-plus targetIndia A's successful chase of 250 in 14.2 overs is the quickest instance of a team chasing down a target of 200 or more in List A cricket. The previous record belonged to Allied Bank Limited, who had completed a 200-plus chase in 20 overs against Service Industries in Lahore during the 2003 Patron's Cup. India A bettered that mark by almost six overs, producing a remarkable batting display to seal the contest.The team also registered the quickest 100 in List A cricket, reaching the milestone in just five overs. New Zealand previously held the record after scoring 100 in 6.3 overs against Sri Lanka in Christchurch in 2015. India A also went past their own effort of 6.3 overs against Sri Lanka A in Dambulla in 2026, while New Zealand's 6.4-over effort against England in Wellington in 2015 features among the fastest team hundreds.Quickest team 100 in List A one day cricket5 overs India A vs UAE Doha 20266.3 NZ vs SL Christchurch 20156.3 India A vs SL A Dambulla 20266.4 NZ vs England Wellington 2015India A's six-hitting display was equally remarkable, with the team smashing 31 maximums during the chase. It is the second-highest number of sixes hit by a team in a List A innings, behind Bihar's record of 38 against Arunachal Pradesh in Ranchi in 2025. Sooryavanshi accounted for 28 of India's sixes.Sooryavanshi's 204 headlines India's record-breaking chaseSooryavanshi smashed 204 off just 53 deliveries, with his innings featuring seven fours and 28 sixes. He brought up his century in just 28 balls before completing his double hundred in 53 deliveries, adding another landmark performance to his growing list of records.Earlier, UAE had posted 249/8 in their 50 overs, with Harpreet Singh Bhatia leading the innings with a brilliant 130 off 144 balls. However, Sooryavanshi's explosive knock completely changed the complexion of the contest as India A raced to 254/3 in just 14.2 overs to register a dominant seven-wicket win.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Six maara kya?': Tilak Varma reveals India A dugout's hilarious reaction to Sooryavanshi's 204-run carnage
articles.summary: India A captain Tilak Varma was left short of words after witnessing Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's breathtaking 204-run assault against the UAE in the ACC Men's
articles.body: India A captain Tilak Varma was left short of words after witnessing Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's breathtaking 204-run assault against the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026. Describing the youngster's innings as "absolute carnage", Tilak admitted that the contest was virtually over within the first five overs of India's chase.Sooryavanshi produced one of the most destructive batting performances in List A cricket, smashing 204 off just 53 deliveries, including seven fours and a record-breaking 28 sixes. His extraordinary knock helped India A chase down a target of 250 in just 14.2 overs, securing a dominant seven-wicket victory.'The match was done in first five overs': TilakSpeaking after the match, Tilak was full of admiration for the teenager's fearless approach and the manner in which he continued his assault after giving India A a flying start."No words to describe him. I would only say it was absolute carnage. The way he played, I think the match was done in the first five overs. We were at 100 in five overs, and the way he carried on after that was tremendous to watch," Tilak said.The India A skipper also offered a glimpse into the atmosphere inside the dugout as Sooryavanshi continued to send the UAE bowlers on a leather hunt. With the youngster clearing the boundary almost at will, the players were thoroughly enjoying the spectacle rather than worrying about the state of the chase.Tilak revealed that the only instruction coming from the dugout was to keep attacking, with the players repeatedly shouting, "Maar, maaro, maaro.""Honestly, there wasn't much to it. Everyone knows how well he can hit sixes. So when he was going like that, everyone was saying, as they say in India, 'Maar, maaro, maaro.' That's all. Everyone was just enjoying and watching," he added.The captain further revealed that Sooryavanshi's six-hitting spree had become the biggest talking point in the dugout, with the players barely paying attention to his boundaries."Even when the ball went for four, nobody was really looking at it. Everyone was asking, 'Six maara kya? Six maara kya?' That's how it was. It was a very good innings, tremendous to watch, one of the best innings," Tilak said.India A vs UAE: How the match unfoldedEarlier, UAE posted 249/8 in their allotted 50 overs after being asked to bat. Harpreet Singh Bhatia anchored the innings with a magnificent 130 off 144 balls, striking 12 fours and four sixes. Basil Hameed also made a valuable contribution, remaining unbeaten on 36 off 36 deliveries. Arshad Khan was the standout bowler for India A, claiming four wickets for 43 runs.However, UAE's competitive total proved nowhere near enough as Sooryavanshi launched an astonishing counterattack. The left-handed opener reached his century in just 28 balls before completing his double century in 53 deliveries. He eventually departed for 204, having smashed 28 sixes in an innings that rewrote several List A records.India A raced to 254/3 in just 14.2 overs, with Rinku Singh remaining unbeaten on 21. The seven-wicket victory was headlined by Sooryavanshi's extraordinary innings, which also helped India A register the quickest successful chase of a 200-plus target in List A cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: From fastest double century to most sixes: List of records Vaibhav Sooryavanshi shattered with his 204 against UAE
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages as he rewrote the record books with a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the ACC
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages as he rewrote the record books with a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday. The 15-year-old India A opener smashed 28 sixes and seven fours, registering one of the most extraordinary batting performances in professional cricket.Sooryavanshi's incredible knock helped India A chase down a target of 250 in just 14.2 overs, securing a seven-wicket victory. In the process, the youngster broke multiple records across List A and professional cricket, setting new benchmarks for batting strike rates, fastest centuries, double centuries and six-hitting.Here is a look at the records Sooryavanshi created with his sensational innings.1. Highest strike rate in a List A centurySooryavanshi registered a staggering strike rate of 384.90, the highest ever in a List A innings featuring a century. He surpassed former South Africa captain AB de Villiers, who had held the record for over a decade after scoring 149 off 44 balls at a strike rate of 338.63 against the West Indies in Johannesburg in 2015.Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk occupies the third position with his 125 off 38 balls at a strike rate of 328.94 for South Australia against Tasmania in 2023.2. Fastest double century in List A cricketThe India A opener smashed the fastest double century in List A cricket, reaching the 200-run mark in just 52 balls. He comfortably surpassed the previous record held by Chad Bowes, who had taken 103 deliveries to score a double century for Canterbury against Otago in Christchurch in 2024.Tamil Nadu's N Jagadeesan and England's Harry Brook are next on the list, having reached their respective double centuries in 114 balls.3. Most sixes in an innings in professional cricketSooryavanshi smashed an astonishing 28 sixes, setting a new record for the most maximums hit in a single innings across professional cricket. He went past Tanmay Agarwal's previous record of 26 sixes, scored for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in a Ranji Trophy match in 2024.Colin Munro and D'Arcy Short had previously struck 23 sixes each in their respective innings.4. Most sixes in a List A inningsThe teenager also set a new record for the most sixes in a single List A innings with his 28 maximums against the UAE. Australia's D'Arcy Short previously held the record with 23 sixes for Western Australia against Queensland in 2018.Bevon Jacobs is third on the list with 21 sixes for Auckland against Otago in 2026.5. Fastest 150 in List A cricketSooryavanshi reached his 150-run mark in just 40 balls, registering the fastest 150 in List A cricket. Interestingly, he also occupies the second position on the list, having scored 150 in 59 balls for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh in 2025.De Villiers had previously held the record with his 64-ball 150 against the West Indies in Johannesburg in 2015, while Jos Buttler reached the milestone in 65 balls against the Netherlands in 2022.6. Fastest List A centurySooryavanshi brought up his century in just 28 balls, registering the fastest hundred in List A cricket. He broke Jake Fraser-McGurk's record of 29 balls, set for South Australia against Tasmania in 2023.De Villiers had previously held the third spot with his 31-ball century against the West Indies in 2015, while Bihar's Sakibul Gani and Jharkhand's Ishan Kishan had also registered centuries in 32 and 33 balls, respectively.7. Fastest century in his professional careerSooryavanshi's 28-ball hundred against the UAE also became the fastest century of his professional career. His previous best was a 32-ball hundred for India A against the UAE in a T20 match in 2025.He has also scored centuries off 35 balls for Rajasthan Royals against Gujarat Titans in 2025 and 36 balls for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh in List A cricket in 2025, as well as for Rajasthan Royals against Sunrisers Hyderabad in 2026.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ben ‌Stokes: Former England captain registers for 2027 Indian ‌Premier League auction
articles.summary: Ben Stokes has entered his name for the 2027 IPL auction; former England captain is among 30 players listed at the maximum base price of INR 2 crore [£165,000]
articles.body:
IPL rules barred players ​who skipped the mega auction in 2025 from registering for the ​following mini auction, ⁠meaning Stokes could ⁠not return to the auction pool until ‌2027.

Indian media reported, however, that the 35-year-old has been ‌granted permission by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to enter this ⁠year's auction.

The 35-year-old has been listed at the maximum base price of INR 2 crore [£165,000] with the players' auction held next month, a day before England's first Test on their tour of South Africa, live on Sky Sports.

England internationals Jonny Bairstow, Sam Billings, Sonny Baker and Tom Curran are also in the 30-player group with the maximum base price.

Stokes, who retired ​from international cricket ​this year, last played ​for Chennai Super Kings in ⁠2023 and has scored 935 runs and taken ⁠28 wickets in ​45 IPL matches across five ​seasons.

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi breaks AB de Villiers' long-standing record with historic 204 off 53 against UAE
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripted another slice of cricket history with his sensational 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripted another slice of cricket history with his sensational 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday. The India A opener registered a staggering strike rate of 384.90, surpassing the long-standing record held by former South Africa captain AB de Villiers for the highest strike rate in a List A innings featuring a century.De Villiers had held the record since January 2015, when he smashed 149 off just 44 deliveries against the West Indies in Johannesburg at a strike rate of 338.63. Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk occupied the third spot with his 125 off 38 balls at a strike rate of 328.94 for South Australia against Tasmania in 2023.Sooryavanshi's remarkable knock featured seven fours and 28 sixes. He brought up his century in just 28 balls before completing his double century in 53 deliveries, producing one of the most destructive innings in List A cricket.His extraordinary batting display also powered India A to a dominant seven-wicket victory. Chasing 250, India A reached 254/3 in just 14.2 overs, turning the contest into a one-sided affair.Highest strike rates in List A centuriesPlayerScoreStrike rateVaibhav Sooryavanshi204 off 53384.90AB de Villiers149 off 44338.63Jake Fraser-McGurk125 off 38328.94India A thrash UAE by seven-wicketsIndia A registered a stunning seven-wicket victory over UAE in their Rising Stars Asia Cup clash, chasing down a target of 250 in just 14.2 overs. UAE had posted 249/8 in their 50 overs, with Harpreet Singh Bhatia leading the innings with a brilliant 130 off 144 balls, including 12 fours and four sixes. Basil Hameed also chipped in with an unbeaten 36 off 36 deliveries, while Arshad Khan was the pick of the Indian bowlers, claiming four wickets for 43 runs.However, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi completely took the game away from UAE with a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls. The youngster smashed seven fours and a record-breaking 28 sixes, reaching his century in just 28 deliveries before completing his double century off 53 balls.
